title: Prototype Report
description:
The evidence package for gate G4 — the kill gate.

Its job is to make an honest kill possible. That means it must evaluate each kill criterion authored at strategy time with a MEASURED value, and it must carry playtest observations from someone who had not seen the game before. A report that only describes what was built cannot support a decision to stop.

The recommendation field is the producing role's view, not the verdict. The verdict is a decision-record.

1.1.0 adds two things the gate needs in order to read the build against the design rather than against itself: `design_gaps`, every place the design did not say enough to build from and what was assumed instead, which is how a design is corrected rather than silently reinterpreted; and `content_coverage`, how many of the designed content units were built, partly built or cut - a prototype that built two of six levels is not a prototype of the design.

1.2.0 adds `specialist`: a develop visit the triage step routed to a specialist records which one, the findings it was given and what its sessions cost; the next triage records what the gates measured of them (triage-report `ledger`).

url.description: A playable build a reviewer can open unaided.

iteration.description: Checked against title_strategy.max_prototype_iterations so ITERATE cannot become an unbounded polish loop.

proved.description: One entry per item in title_strategy.prototype_must_prove. The prototype exists to answer these; anything else built is scope that was not asked for.

kill_criteria_eval.description: Every criterion from title-strategy, with what was actually measured. Omitting one is how a kill gate quietly stops working.

playtest_sessions.description: At scale this is the vertical slice review, so the bar is 'a stranger played it', not 'the mechanic runs'.

player_context.description: First-time sessions are the ones that count. Internal sessions cannot tell you whether the game is understandable.

integration_status.description: The prototype must prove integration, not just gameplay. Deferring SDK and monetization wiring to production is how titles discover at release that the placement does not fit the loop.

scope_deltas.description: What was built that the plan did not call for, or planned and not built. Surfaced rather than absorbed silently.

design_gaps.description: Every place the design did not say enough to build from, with the question it left open and what was assumed instead. Added in 1.1.0, and read back by title:design: a gap recorded here is a design fix, not a note. A blocking gap is one the prototype could not be built honestly around.

field.description: The path into the game-design that is missing or ambiguous, e.g. build_spec.content.units[l-03].success, build_spec.difficulty.axes[speed].range.

question.description: What the developer needed to know, as a question the designer can answer.

assumed.description: What was built instead, or null when the gap stopped the work.

severity.description: blocking: the thing could not be built as designed. minor: an assumption was made and should be confirmed.

unit.description: The content unit id the gap is in, when it is in one.

specialist.description: Added in 1.2.0. The specialist this visit was briefed as, when the triage step routed it (docs/specialist-routing.md): the role (core/roles/roles.yaml), the ids of the quality findings it was given - only those it owns - the triage-report that routed them, and the developer sessions this visit spent and their cost as the run's budget recorded them (null when unknown). Whether each finding was resolved is measured afterwards, by the gate that raised it, and recorded in the next triage-report's ledger.

pending.description: The specialists still to visit this build after this one, in order.

source.description: The gate entry the findings came from (verify.fail, visual-qa.develop, prototype-review.iterate, ...).

content_coverage.description: The designed content against the built content: how many units the design specified and how many the prototype actually carries. Added in 1.1.0. `designed` counts the units of the tier this prototype was asked for; a report where built is far below designed says the prototype is of a smaller game than the one reviewed.

built.description: Units built to their acceptance criteria.

partial.description: Units present but not meeting every acceptance line.

units.description: Per unit, so the count can be checked rather than believed.

rationale.description: Sunk cost is not a rationale. The question is whether we would start this today knowing what we now know.
